notes: Source 4 = Netzer 1975, Qadmoniot (Hebrew); quotes are from the packet's English translation. The site has a summit and a lower terrace 'about 30 m below it on the south-east side' (p. 56). Summit features in the bathhouse 'in the north-western corner of the summit' are coded NW from the site. s4f1-s4f2 are the Hasmonean pool and cistern that the p. 58 caption puts under the tepidarium of that bathhouse. s4f7: the lower bathhouse is 'in the north-eastern corner' of the lower terrace (pp. 59-60), a direction within the terrace rather than from the site as a whole, so relative_to other. The terrace lies SE of the summit. On the general plan (p. 55; north arrow to the upper right) this bathhouse lies roughly E-ESE of the summit. But the plan has no coordinates and the unit's recorded point cannot be placed on it, so there is no plan position. The p. 60 caption 'two pools of the caldarium' is taken to show the same two stepped pools, not further pools. s4f8: the four cisterns are 'on the east ... at the foot of the hill'. Not taken as Nigro N32 (585 m NNE, 'aqueducts & cisterns'), because the place is not clearly the same. s4f6: two cisterns, coded as one feature; dated D because the source assigns all summit remains to the Hasmonean and Herodian periods. Not coded: the stone bathtubs and the marble labrum (vessels, not pools); Meshel's aqueduct to the foot of the hill. No graves are mentioned. The bathhouse plans (p. 59) have no north arrow.
